rounds.analysis: L21h6 looks like a successor head. Ablating it gives the largest drop in next-item margin. In the oracle, feeding it the value vector from one item later gives two-steps-ahead answers 97% of the time, so its OV circuit maps an attended item to that item's successor. It barely attends to the queried value in lookups (0.03). Hypothesis: if its QK is reprogrammed so the final position attends to the queried value token, its existing OV will write the successor. Copy heads such as L22h7 and L16h14 will compete by writing the plain value. This round tests three things: the bare reprogramming (A), whether boosting output gain is needed (B), and whether removing the late copy head L22h7 shifts answers from lookup to successor (C). I use the low rope band so attention does not depend on distance, and contrast against other values so the head picks the queried line's value specifically.

candidates.rationale: Base hypothesis: reprogramming only L21h6's attention to the queried value is enough for its successor OV to produce the next item.

rounds.analysis:
Round 1: reprogramming L21h6 raised its attention to the queried value only from 0.03 to 0.16. The successor rate fell (0.315 to 0.21) and sequence continuation dropped to 0.9, so the new QK probably also broke h6's normal sequence pattern. The closed-form attention map at ridge 0.1 / rank 32 / low band is too weak. Three ways to get more attention onto the value:
(A) Borrow an existing lookup QK. L21h8 attends 0.27 to the queried value, so copy its QK into h6 and keep h6's successor OV. This tests whether a natural lookup pattern plus the successor OV is enough.
(B) Stronger closed form: low ridge, full rank 64, other_positions contrast. Add gain on h6 and remove the late copy head L22h7.
(C) Use all 128 dims, so rotary distance can help pick the value line, with lower ridge and moderate gain.
Check WikiText cost from gains, since h6 matters for WikiText (+0.051 when removed).

candidates.rationale: Mechanism test: give the successor head the QK of a head in the same layer that already attends to the queried value (L21h8, 0.27). If the successor rate rises, the OV hypothesis holds and closed-form attention was the bottleneck.
Sharper closed-form attention (ridge 0.01, rank 64, contrast against all other positions). Boost h6's output and remove L22h7 to cut the competing plain-value copy.
Full-band program so rotary position can help localize the queried line, with lower ridge, other_values contrast and moderate gain. Compares the 'all' band with the 'low' band at matched ridge.

rounds.analysis: Rounds 1-2: retargeting L21h6's QK never pushed its attention on the queried value above 0.16. It also cost sequence continuation and WikiText, because h6 matters for both. Copying L21h8's QK into h6 nudged the successor rate up (0.325). Lowering the ridge made attention weaker, not stronger (0.1 at ridge 0.1 vs 0.16 at 0.01), so a larger ridge may sharpen it. New hypothesis: route the other way. Keep h6 intact and give its successor OV to heads that already attend to the queried value (L21h8 0.27, L21h15 0.27) via copy_ov. Caveats: this also changes the values of h9 and h14, which share those value groups. I also don't know how far h6's OV map depends on its original value rows, but copy_ov transfers value rows and output columns together, so the map should carry over. Programme C checks the ridge direction with a high-ridge, low-rank closed form on h6.

candidates.rationale: Mechanism test: put the successor OV on the two layer-21 heads that already attend to the queried value, and leave h6 untouched to protect sequences and WikiText.
Same transplant with output gain on both heads, to see whether the successor signal is strength-limited against the copy heads.
Ridge-direction test: lower ridge reduced attention, so try a strongly regularised, low-rank, low-band map on h6 with modest gain.

rounds.analysis: Round 3 gave two levers. (1) A high-ridge, low-rank closed form on h6 doubled attention on the queried value (0.27) and gave the best successor rate (0.55). It cost sequence continuation (0.5) because h6's own pattern is overwritten, and raised WikiText to 2.997 (+5.8%, still eligible). (2) Transplanting h6's OV to the natural lookup heads h8 and h15 is cheap (WikiText 2.854, sequences intact), and gain helps (0.46). Tests this round: (A) whether the two levers add. (B) A dedicated-head version: closed-form attention plus h6's OV on a WikiText-irrelevant head (h4, group 2; h5 shares the value group, and removing either costs nothing). This leaves h6 untouched, so sequences and WikiText should be preserved. (C) Whether raising the ridge further (10) keeps sharpening h6's attention.

candidates.rationale: Additivity test: retarget h6 with the best closed form (ridge 3, rank 16) and also transplant its OV to h8 and h15 with gain 2. Several attending heads then write the successor against the copy heads.

Dedicated successor head: build a new lookup head on L21h4 (unimportant for WikiText) with the high-ridge closed form and give it h6's OV. Also transplant the OV to h8 and h15. h6 stays intact, so sequence continuation and WikiText should hold. If the successor rate stays high, the closed form generalises to an arbitrary head.

Ridge-direction test: repeat round 3's h6 programme with ridge raised from 3 to 10, everything else the same (rank 16, low band, other_values, gain 1.5). This shows whether attention and the successor rate keep rising with regularisation.

rounds.analysis: Best so far is round 4 programme 0 at 0.645 successor rate. It combines the ridge-3/rank-16 closed form on h6 at gain 1.5 with h6's OV transplanted to h8 and h15 at gain 2. Its WikiText loss is 3.047 (+7.6%), under the eligibility cap of 2.833 × 1.15 ≈ 3.258. Raising the ridge to 10 kept attention (0.26) but lost successor rate, so ridge 3 stays fixed. The dedicated L21h4 head cost a lot of WikiText, so I drop it. In round 3 the successor signal was strength-limited: gain raised the rate from 0.385 to 0.46 at almost no WikiText cost. This final round pushes gains on the best programme within the WikiText budget. (A) Moderate extra gain on all three heads. (B) Gain only on the cheap transplant heads h8 and h15. (C) The best programme with the downstream copy head L22h7 removed, testing whether plain-value copying still competes. Watch WikiText against the 3.258 cap.

candidates.rationale: Best programme with more gain on all three successor-writing heads (h6 2.0, h8/h15 2.5), to win more of the competition against the copy heads.
Keep h6 at gain 1.5 and put the extra gain only on the transplant heads h8/h15 (gain 3), which have been cheap for WikiText.
Best programme plus removal of the downstream copy head L22h7 (0.41 attention on the queried value). This tests whether plain-value copying after layer 21 still competes with the successor heads.
